properties.name: 1883 Krakatau Volcanic Eruption & Tsunami
properties.description: Cataclysmic volcanic eruption of Krakatau culminating in caldera collapse, atmospheric shockwaves, global temperature reduction, and destructive tsunamis.
properties.evidence_description: Documented 1883 eruption logs, tide gauge sea-level records, barometric shockwave traces, and coastal tsunami inundation surveys.
properties.evidence_significance: Tide gauge and barometric instrument logs provide historical record evidence supporting catastrophic caldera collapse and tsunami generation.
properties.geological_explanation: Paroxysmal eruption and collapse of the Krakatau volcanic island structure displaced huge ocean water masses, creating tsunamis over 30 meters high along Sunda Strait coastal shores.
properties.why_it_matters: The 1883 Krakatau eruption was one of the first globally recorded natural disasters. It demonstrated how volcanic caldera collapse can trigger ocean-wide tsunamis and global atmospheric cooling.
properties.source: Self (1884) / NOAA NCEI Historical Tsunami Database
properties.geometry_note: Point-based representation of Krakatau island epicenter

properties.name: 2004 Indian Ocean Earthquake & Tsunami
properties.description: A massive Mw 9.1 megathrust earthquake off northern Sumatra that generated catastrophic ocean-wide tsunamis affecting coastal Indian Ocean communities.
properties.evidence_description: Global seismic network broadband seismograms, satellite altimetry seafloor displacement measurements, and coastal tsunami inundation field logs.
properties.evidence_significance: Instrumental seismograms and GPS displacement measurements provide quantitative evidence supporting massive megathrust subduction fault rupture.
properties.geological_explanation: A 1,300 km long seafloor fault rupture along the Sunda Megathrust subduction zone rapidly uplifted ocean floor sediment by several meters, transferring immense energy into ocean waves.
properties.why_it_matters: The 2004 Sumatra-Andaman earthquake reshaped modern seismology and tsunami science, demonstrating the devastating energy release of subduction megathrust ruptures and driving the creation of global tsunami warning networks.
properties.source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program (Event ID official20041226005853450_30)

properties.name: 2006 Yogyakarta Earthquake
properties.description: A shallow Mw 6.3 intraplate strike-slip earthquake centered south of Yogyakarta near the Opak Fault zone, causing major structural damage in Bantul.
properties.evidence_description: Strong-motion accelerograph records, shallow Opak fault lineament mapping, and structural damage surveys across Bantul sediment basins.
properties.evidence_significance: Instrumental ground motion records and fault mapping provide evidence consistent with shallow intraplate strike-slip faulting in sediment basins.
properties.geological_explanation: Tectonic stress release along a shallow strike-slip fault system produced severe high-frequency ground motion across soft volcanic sediment and alluvial soils of the Opak River basin.
properties.why_it_matters: The 2006 Yogyakarta earthquake highlighted the vulnerability of volcanic sediment basins to shallow intraplate fault rupture, emphasizing the importance of microzonation and earthquake-resistant engineering.
properties.source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program (Event ID usp000ekfv)

properties.name: 1992 Flores Earthquake & Tsunami
properties.description: A major Mw 7.8 back-arc subduction thrust earthquake off northern Flores that triggered destructive coastal tsunamis up to 26 meters high.
properties.evidence_description: Teleseismic fault-plane solutions, field tsunami runup elevation measurements (up to 26 m), and coastal damage field logs.
properties.evidence_significance: Seismograms and coastal runup surveys provide physical evidence supporting back-arc thrust faulting and localized tsunami displacement.
properties.geological_explanation: A shallow back-arc thrust fault rupture along the Flores Thrust zone displaced sea floor water, producing catastrophic localized tsunami runup along the Maumere coastline.
properties.why_it_matters: The 1992 Flores event demonstrated that back-arc thrust faulting north of the Sunda Arc can generate localized megathrust-scale earthquakes and severe coastal tsunamis.
properties.source: USGS Earthquake Hazards Program / Tsuji et al. (1995)

properties.name: 2018 Palu Earthquake, Liquefaction & Tsunami
properties.description: A Mw 7.5 strike-slip earthquake along the Palu-Koro Fault that triggered severe soil liquefaction and bay-confined submarine landslide tsunamis.
properties.evidence_description: InSAR satellite surface deformation maps, flow liquefaction landslide field surveys in Petobo/Balaroa, and Palu Bay tsunami tide logs.
properties.evidence_significance: Satellite radar deformation and field damage surveys provide direct evidence for complex strike-slip liquefaction and bay tsunami interactions.
properties.geological_explanation: Strike-slip faulting caused extreme shaking in saturated alluvial sediments leading to flow liquefaction, while coastal submarine slope failures displaced Palu Bay waters.
properties.why_it_matters: The 2018 Palu event highlighted complex multi-hazard interactions, where strike-slip faulting caused severe urban liquefaction and bay-confined submarine landslide tsunamis.
